raw_response:
1. The figure does not show any confidence intervals or error bars, so you can’t infer statistical indistinguishability from overlap at higher TFLOPs. It only shows mean loss curves.

2. SepLLM is not ~2.60 at 1.23e9 TFLOPs; it’s closer to ~2.47–2.48, while Vanilla at the same TFLOPs is about ~2.50, so SepLLM is lower by roughly ~0.02–0.03.

3. The plot only goes to about 1.25e9 TFLOPs and provides no confidence intervals, so a 1.5e9 TFLOPs projection and alignment with intervals are not supported by the figure. If you extrapolate the last segment visually, Vanilla might be ~2.49–2.50 and SepLLM ~2.46–2.47, but this is speculative.
